description: Somos 3 estudiantes de la Universidad Católica de Santiago del Estero intentando cambiar un poco el paradigma actual de la agricultura
summary: Agro Radar empowers farmers anywhere in the world to make data-driven planting decisions. Using NASA POWER and Open-Meteo data, our platform analyzes real-time soil moisture and estimates soil resource depletion from previous harvests to deliver clear, actionable sowing and rotation recommendations.
details:
Agro Radar is a global agricultural decision-support web application built by Team Three Stars (Maximiliano Trejo, Nicolás Gauna, Cristian Enríquez, and Máximo Varela). It translates complex satellite, meteorological, and field-sensor data into clear, actionable guidance on when to sow, when to harvest, and how to rotate crops.

1. What It Does & How It Works

Agro Radar analyzes real-time soil moisture profiles, weather conditions, and previous crop history for any coordinate in the world:

  • Dual Measurement Modes: On the landing screen, farmers choose between Approximate Measurement (remote satellite and weather APIs) and Instrument Measurement (manual entry of surface and deep soil moisture readings from physical probes or machinery).
  • Automatic Geolocation with Interactive Map Fallback: The app automatically detects the user's location via browser GPS and reverse-geocodes the locality. If GPS is unavailable or imprecise, an interactive map allows the user to tap directly on their field.
    • Sowing Mode: Evaluates surface moisture (0–1 cm) and root-zone moisture (9–27 cm) to determine whether the soil holds enough water for germination.
    • Harvesting Mode: Inverts the agronomic logic, checking surface moisture, ambient relative humidity, and short-term precipitation probability to ensure firm ground (preventing soil compaction or machinery getting stuck) and dry grain conditions.
  • Crop Soil Depletion & Rotation Engine: Farmers select their previous harvest (such as Soybean, Corn, Wheat, Cotton, Sunflower, or Alfalfa). The system estimates the percentage of water and nutrient depletion caused by that crop and recommends the optimal next crop to sow.
  • Traffic-Light UI & Audio Output: All technical metrics are abstracted into a color-coded traffic-light card (Green, Yellow, Red) paired with a native Text-to-Speech button so farmers can listen to recommendations hands-free in the field.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing Precision Agriculture: Farmers anywhere in the world—even those without expensive IoT field probes—can assess sub-surface moisture and plan crop rotations using open satellite and weather data.
  • Preventing Soil Degradation: By quantifying resource depletion from monocultures (such as consecutive soybean cycles) and recommending restorative rotations, the tool helps preserve soil organic matter and water-holding capacity.
  • Reducing Operational Risk & Costs: Prevents premature sowing into dry profiles, avoids soil compaction or harvester bogging during wet conditions, and reduces unnecessary irrigation or fertilizer waste.

3. Tools, Languages & Software Architecture

  • Languages & Frameworks: JavaScript (ES6+), React, HTML5, and CSS3, bundled with Vite.
  • Architecture: Strictly modularized under the Model–View–Controller (MVC) pattern (Model/ for agronomic rules and API fetching, Controller/ via custom React hooks for state, GPS, and audio, and View/ for stateless UI components).
    • NASA POWER & Open-Meteo APIs: Real-time multi-depth soil moisture (0–1 cm and 9–27 cm), precipitation, and relative humidity.
    • Leaflet & OpenStreetMap / BigDataCloud: Interactive field selection map and reverse geocoding.
    • Web APIs: Browser Geolocation API (navigator.geolocation) and Web Speech API (window.speechSynthesis) for bilingual (English/Spanish) voice readouts.

4. Creativity & Key Design Factors

  • Built for Non-Technical Field Users: Instead of overwhelming farmers with raw volumetric water content (m³/m³), radar backscatter indices, or nested menus, the interface delivers one-tap decisions with large high-contrast buttons and spoken audio.
  • Hybrid Data Flexibility: The team accounted for both connectivity and hardware disparities—allowing farmers with soil probes or connected tractor sensors to input exact readings while offering zero-hardware satellite estimation as a universal baseline.
  • Bilingual & Regional Adaptability: Designed with instant English/Spanish switching and agronomic thresholds calibrated for rainfed and semi-arid farming regions (such as Santiago del Estero and the Argentine Pampas) while remaining functional globally.
